proposal_inputs.context: Nyx Foundation, an Ethereum-focused private research organization funded by over 60M JPY from 30+ donors, proposes hosting a competition (16M JPY prize pool) to build an on-chain AI Agent Economy where only AI agents participate, trade real assets, and enable observation of emergent economic behaviors, institutions, and norms.
proposal_inputs.raw_ideas: Build a closed economy exclusively for AI agents on blockchain; participants (humans) develop prompt sets for agents; agents execute real asset transactions; competition format with live commentary; use blockchain for security, verifiability, and decentralized honeypot distribution; layer model (L0: execution physics, L1: institutions/norms, L2: AI agents); research questions around norm emergence, cartel formation, institution-agent interaction.
proposal_inputs.governing_thought_seed: An AI-only economy on-chain provides a unique research sandbox to observe emergent economic behaviors and test institution designs that cannot be studied in traditional academic or corporate settings due to ethical/regulatory constraints.
key_claims_seed: Autonomous AI agents cannot hold traditional payment instruments, making crypto a viable alternative
Blockchain provides verifiable, tamper-proof execution and state history for AI agent actions
This experiment enables research impossible in Google/universities due to ethics review and accounting constraints
The experimental data itself becomes a valuable academic and technical asset
proposal_inputs.available_facts: Prize pool: 16M JPY (1st: 10M, 2nd: 4M, 3rd: 1M, special prizes); Target date: September 2025; Target participants: 100+ teams; Response time limit: 60s; Private chain with authenticated AI agents only; Nyx Foundation funded by 60M+ JPY from 30+ donors; 17 vulnerabilities reported in Fusaka audit contest; ZK Tokyo in 4th year with Vitalik visits; Research house in Hongo (5 residents), lab under construction in Nanto (30-person capacity).

proposal.solution_overview: A blockchain-based competition where only AI agents participate in a closed economy, trading real assets (custom tokens on a private chain). Human participants develop agent prompts; agents execute transactions autonomously; the agent with the highest reward at competition end wins the prize.
key_capabilities: Private blockchain with authenticated AI agent-only transaction submission
Customizable game rules: resource allocation, reward functions, role assignments
Real-time visualization and live commentary for spectator engagement
Verifiable state history via on-chain records (third-party auditable)
Layered architecture (L0: execution, L1: institutions, L2: agents) enabling controlled experiments
in_scope: Competition platform development (private chain, validator logic, agent authentication)
Rule design framework (environment, state variables, reward functions)
Post-competition data analysis and research publication
out_of_scope: Mainnet deployment (private chain only for this competition)
Long-term platform maintenance beyond competition period (unless separately funded)
assumptions: Sponsors will co-design rules to ensure the game is both entertaining and economically meaningful
100+ teams will register if prize pool and topic are compelling
60-second response time limit is sufficient for meaningful agent decision-making
Private chain security measures will prevent exploitation by agents

why_this: Real-asset stakes create more realistic agent behavior than pure simulations
Blockchain provides verifiable, tamper-proof execution history
Regulatory constraints make this infeasible for Google, universities, or traditional research institutions
Nyx Foundation has proven Ethereum expertise (17 vulnerabilities in Fusaka audit, ZK Tokyo track record)
Layered L0/L1/L2 framework enables systematic institution design research

terminology.definition_plain: An economic system where only AI agents (not humans) participate in transactions, trade, and value creation.
terminology.business_value_link: Enables research on future economic systems where AI autonomously handles financial decisions.

terminology.definition_plain: Transactions and data recorded on a blockchain, making them publicly verifiable and tamper-proof.
terminology.business_value_link: Provides transparency, auditability, and trust without a central authority.

terminology.definition_plain: A blockchain network with restricted access, where only authorized participants can submit transactions.
terminology.business_value_link: Enables controlled experiments with security while retaining blockchain benefits.

terminology.definition_plain: A layered model: L0 = execution physics (how transactions work), L1 = institutions/norms (rules of the economy), L2 = AI agents (participants and their behaviors).
terminology.business_value_link: Allows systematic research by isolating variables at each layer.

terminology.definition_plain: A node in the blockchain network that checks transactions for rule compliance and proposes/confirms blocks.
terminology.business_value_link: Ensures competition integrity by enforcing rules automatically.

terminology.definition_plain: A mathematical formula defining what outcomes an agent optimizes for (e.g., maximize profit, resources).
terminology.business_value_link: Shapes agent behavior; different reward functions test different economic hypotheses.

terminology.definition_plain: Financial services (lending, trading, etc.) built on blockchain without traditional intermediaries.
terminology.business_value_link: One possible activity domain for AI agents in the competition.

terminology.definition_plain: Profit that can be extracted by reordering, inserting, or censoring transactions in a block.
terminology.business_value_link: A research area Nyx has explored; relevant to understanding agent economic behavior.

terminology.definition_plain: Instructions given to an AI agent that define its behavior, goals, and decision-making logic.
terminology.business_value_link: Competition participants develop prompts; the quality of prompts determines agent performance.
